newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Dr. Death says he did the right thing.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Dr. Death says he did the right thing.

text.p: Darwin doctor Philip Nitschke said he felt sad but relieved as the Nembutal was injected into the elderly man lying at home in his bed in the sleepy tropical city of Darwin on a sunny Sunday afternoon.

Nitschke, dubbed "Doctor Death" by his critics, had just helped terminal cancer patient Bob Dent administer a lethal injection to become the first man to die under the world's first voluntary euthanasia law.
"You couldn't not be affected by it," Nitschke, who has devoted himself to the controversial pro-euthanasia campaign, told Reuters by telephone from Darwin.
"It couldn't be an average day and it's not the sort of thing you would want to make a habit of -- it certainly took its toll."
Nitschke said he had been worried on Sunday. The atmosphere in Dent's house had at first been tense.
But Dent, 66, who had suffered five long years of agonising pain from prostate cancer, told his doctor the assisted suicide was an act of love.
"I came out of that with a sense that I had done something good," Nitschke said.
"It was a very difficult time for me, but I was left with the overwhelming feeling that I had done the right thing, done something good by being able to end the suffering of this brave man."
Nitschke, who runs his small practice from a tiny backroom in a Darwin industrial zone, has been campaigning for months to secure the signatures he needed to help a patient die under the law.
He has already seen one patient, 66-year-old taxi driver Max Bell, die in agony because he had been unable to find the two doctors and psychiatrist needed to approve a voluntary euthanasia bid.
Nitschke said Dent's death brought him the certainty that he could now help five other patients who have come to him asking to die.
"We had to work damn hard to get this one to work, it's a bloody miracle," he said.
"The next one will be easier. It always gets easier."
Dent died using a computerised euthanasia kit Nitschke invented with the help of a computer buff friend.

The computer poses a series of questions, with the final question being: "If you press 'Yes', you will cause a lethal injection to be given within 30 seconds, and you will die. Do you wish to proceed?"
When Bob Dent pressed "yes", he was injected first with Nembutal, which sent him to sleep, and then a muscle-relaxant, which caused him to die from asphyxiation within minutes.
